one_line: Deified memory of the Nilachal hill’s goddess in the Pala-era Kalika Purana, binding sacred geography, myth, and royal politics around Kamrupa’s Brahmaputra valley.

appearance.age_look: Appears mid-20s, graceful and sturdy, with a calm but commanding presence suited to a hill-goddess and temple’s presiding deity.
appearance.face: Soft heart-shaped face with warm medium-brown complexion, straight nose, full lips, a small red vertical tilak between the brows, and large expressive eyes that usually hold a serene, slightly enigmatic half-smile.
appearance.hair: Long, thick black hair parted at the center, drawn into a high braided bun at the back of the crown and wrapped with a narrow red cloth band, with two loose, gently wavy side-locks framing the cheeks and a few strands tucked behind the ears.
appearance.costume: She wears a modest, fully draped Assamese-style mekhela–sador ensemble: a deep-red cotton mekhela (lower wrap skirt) with narrow woven black and gold temple-border motifs, pleated neatly at the front and reaching the ankles; over it a cream-white sador (upper drape) with a broad red end-panel and thin black horizontal stripes, wrapped over both shoulders and across the torso to cover the upper body completely; beneath, a plain fitted blouse in muted marigold-yellow is just hinted at under the sador; her jewellery is simple but dignified—small round gold earrings, a short gold bead necklace, a slightly longer necklace with a leaf-shaped pendant, and a narrow pair of gold bangles on each wrist; she stays barefoot to evoke the hill shrine, with an ankle-length hem ensuring modesty, and a thin red waist-cord is visible where the sador is tucked at the side.
appearance.signature: A small, era-appropriate copper-plate charter held in her left hand—rectangular, darkened copper with a central ring—representing the Umachal and Hayunthal epigraphs and the later Kalika Purana’s textual memory, while her right hand rests gently on a plain stone yoni-like altar slab partially wrapped in a red cloth as a dignified symbol of the sacred site and its myths rather than any literal sacrifice.

ref_desc: Kamakhya of Nilachal is a mid-20s-looking medium-brown woman with a heart-shaped face, high braided bun wrapped in a red band, Assamese red mekhela and cream-red sador with black borders over a marigold blouse, simple gold jewellery, barefoot, holding a small copper-plate charter and touching a draped stone altar, in deep red, cream white, black, marigold yellow and antique gold tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Kamakhya of Nilachal, a dignified medium-brown woman appearing in her mid-20s with a heart-shaped face, large calm eyes, straight nose, and a small red vertical tilak; her long black hair is parted in the center, gathered into a high braided bun at the back, wrapped with a narrow red cloth band, and two loose wavy side-locks frame her cheeks. She wears a fully modest Assamese mekhela–sador outfit: a deep-red cotton mekhela reaching her ankles, with narrow woven black and gold temple-border motifs, neatly pleated at the front; over it a cream-white sador with a broad red end-panel and thin black horizontal stripes, wrapped across her torso and over both shoulders, completely covering her upper body and hinting only subtly at a plain marigold-yellow blouse underneath. Her jewellery is restrained—small round gold earrings, a short gold bead necklace, a slightly longer necklace with a leaf-shaped pendant, and narrow gold bangles on each wrist; she is barefoot to suggest the sacred hill, with the mekhela and sador keeping her fully covered and modest. In her left hand she holds a small era-accurate copper-plate charter, rectangular and darkened, with a central ring, and her right hand rests gently on a simple stone yoni-like altar slab that is fully draped in a red cloth, symbolizing the shrine’s sacred focus rather than any graphic ritual. Use a rich but grounded palette of deep red, cream white, black, marigold yellow, and antique gold, and show her in neutral standing poses from multiple angles to fix her hairstyle, garments, jewellery, copper plate, and the small draped stone altar as her consistent design elements.
